title: The Ill child in the back room
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：ill　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ill 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the herder wrote of ① an ill child in the back room in the ledger, and everybody in the pasture said at once that it was ② worse than the one named there the year before. Three winters on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the herder, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the ill ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the worst child in the back room anybody in the pasture had ever seen, or so the ledger for December 1975 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too ill to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the neighbour who had come to help; the ill ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far pen, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an ill wind from the north, and said that no neighbour in his right mind would call it ⑥ as ill as the wind from the north they had once had in the old pasture. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was ill or not, and he said so.

By 1988 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the ledger. What the line asked for was ⑦ something ill, and nothing besides. The neighbour from the next pasture called the whole plan ⑧ quite ill; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the ledger kept the names of the ill ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1991, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another ill child in the back room in the same ledger, and the work, which took two winters, seemed ⑨ worse than anybody had expected. ⑩ The worst wind from the north in the whole pasture, she said in 1993, was the one she could never quite name; the ill ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 生病（前置定语 an ill child in the back room：1981 年牧人在牧群台账里记下的那件生病的小孩）
B. adj. 生病／不良（比较级 worse than：文中两处，一处比后屋生病的小孩，一处比预想）
C. adj. 生病／不良（最高级 the worst：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 生病（表语 too ill to do：母亲觉得它太生病，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 不良（前置定语 an ill wind from the north：叔叔把整件事称作一桩不良的邪风）
F. adj. 不良（同级比较 as ill as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩北面吹来的邪风相比）
G. adj. 不良（后置定语 something ill：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 不良（受程度副词修饰 quite ill：那位邻人的评价）

items.q: an ill child in the back room
the worst child in the back room anybody
an ill wind from the north
The worst wind from the north in

answers.why: ill 意为“生病”，1981 年牧人在牧群台账里记下的是“一件生病的小孩”，此处作前置定语 an ill child in the back room。
ill 意为“生病”，此处用比较级 worse than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
ill 意为“生病”，牧群台账上 十二月 那行字说它是牧场里最生病的一件，故用最高级 the worst child in the back room。
ill 意为“生病”，母亲认为这件东西“太生病了，谁也用不上”，too ill to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
ill 意为“不良”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩不良的邪风”，此处作前置定语 an ill wind from the north。
ill 意为“不良”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩北面吹来的邪风一样不良”，同级比较用 as ill as。
ill 意为“不良”，牧群台账上那半行字要的是“不良的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something ill。
ill 意为“不良”，邻牧场来的那位邻人认为这套计划“相当不良”，quite 修饰原级 ill。
ill 意为“不良”，1991 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要不良”，故用比较级 worse than。
ill 意为“不良”，母亲 1993 年说的是“整个牧场里最不良的那一桩”，故用最高级 the worst wind from the north。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1981 年，牧人在牧群台账里记下了一件生病的小孩。（an ill child in the back room）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更生病。（worse than …）
母亲觉得它太生病，谁也用不上。（too ill to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩不良的邪风。（an ill wind from the north）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩北面吹来的邪风一样不良。（as ill as …）
到了 1988 年，牧群台账上只剩半行字：要的是一件不良的东西。（something ill）
answers: In 1981 the herder wrote of an ill child in the back room in the ledger.
Everybody said it was worse than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too ill to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an ill wind from the north.
He said nobody would call it as ill as the wind from the north they had once had.
By 1988 the ledger asked for nothing but something ill.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 ill 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1981 the herder wrote of an ill child in the back room in the ledger, and nobody forgot it.
It was the worst child in the back room in the pasture, or so the ledger says.
My mother thought it too ill to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an ill wind from the north, and nobody argued with him.
The neighbour from the next pasture called the plan quite ill, and everybody laughed.
The ill ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
